- Management fee, based on end-of-year AUM before fees: 1.5%
- Incentive fee: 20%

cache_stem: An analyst gathers the following information about a hedge fund: Beginning-of-year assets under management (AUM) €200 million, Management fee, based on end-of-year AUM before fees 1.5%, Incentive fee 20%, Hard hurdle rate 5%, Annual return before fees 15%. If the incentive fee is based on returns net of management fees, total fees for the year are closest to:
db_expl:
Management fee = 1.5% x end-of-year AUM before fees. End-of-year AUM before fees = €200m x 1.15 = €230m, so management fee = €230m x 1.5% = €3.45m.

Return net of management fees = (€230m - €3.45m - €200m) / €200m = €26.55m / €200m = 13.275%.

Incentive fee is earned on the return in excess of the 5% hard hurdle rate: (13.275% - 5%) = 8.275% of €200m = €16.55m. Incentive fee = 20% x €16.55m = €3.31m.

Total fees = Management fee + Incentive fee = €3.45m + €3.31m = €6.76m ≈ €6.8 million.
cache_expl: The partnership agreement specifies that the performance fee is earned only after the fund achieves a return known as a hurdle rate, and the correct calculation nets the management fees and applies the hard hurdle rate before calculating the 20% incentive fee.
